source.title: Open problems in microscopic theory of large-amplitude collective motion

accepted.question_text: When oblate and prolate Hartree-Fock-Bogoliubov shape minima coexist in the same nucleus without an exact discrete symmetry relating them, what are the correct collective degree or degrees of freedom that mediate the large-amplitude shape-mixing dynamics between those two configurations, and how can a microscopic theory identify and describe those coordinates?

evidence.quote: In this case, we do not know the relevant collective degree(s) of freedom through which the two shapes mix.
It is obviously needed to develop a microscopic theory capable of describing the shape mixing dynamics of this kind.

accepted.question_text: For the unusually low first excited 0+ states observed in nuclei such as 72Ge, what is the correct microscopic interpretation of those states, and how should one reconcile or distinguish the boson-expansion picture based on coupling between quadrupole anharmonic vibration and neutron pairing vibration from the phenomenological shape-coexistence interpretation?

evidence.quote: The nature of this state is poorly understood.
Relations between the two interpretations are not well understood.

accepted.question_text: What microscopic mechanism produces the oblate-prolate asymmetry in nuclear structure, meaning the empirical tendency for prolate shapes to be energetically favored over oblate shapes in many nuclei, especially in gamma-soft situations where large-amplitude shape mixing can easily wash out separate rotational-band identities?

evidence.quote: In spite of the obvious importance for understanding low-energy collective spectra, the microscopic origin of the oblate-prolate asymmetry in nuclear structure (the reason why the prolate shapes are energetically more favored in many cases than the oblate shapes) still remains as one of the long-standing and fundamental problems.
It may be interesting to apply this approach to the problem in question for a deeper understanding of the oblate-prolate asymmetry.

accepted.question_text: In the generator coordinate method for quadrupole collective phenomena, how reliable are the collective masses or inertia functions computed using real generator coordinates, and how should one choose or determine the generator coordinates so that the resulting collective description captures both the coordinates and the momenta needed for correct large-amplitude dynamics?

evidence.quote: A long-standing open problem in the GCM is the reliability of the collective masses (inertia functions) evaluated with the real generator coordinates.
Another important problem in the GCM is the choice of the generator coordinates.

accepted.question_text: How large are the contributions of time-odd mean-field components induced by the time evolution of the mean field to the collective mass in large-amplitude collective motion, and how can those effects be evaluated reliably within modern nuclear energy density functionals rather than being omitted as they are in the usual cranking mass?
accepted.context_brief: Time-odd mean-field contributions to collective mass

evidence.quote: In spite of these efforts, it may be fair to say that we are still far from a full understanding of the time-odd effects.
Thus, it remains as a great subject for future to evaluate the time-odd mean-field effects on the collective mass using energy density functionals currently under active development.

accepted.question_text: How should one systematically compare and interpret the different collective masses produced by the ASCC, cranking, GCM-GOA, and ATDHFB approaches, given that the ASCC notion of adiabaticity does not require the collective kinetic energy to be small relative to intrinsic two-quasiparticle excitation energies and therefore differs conceptually from adiabatic perturbation theory?
accepted.context_brief: Comparison of collective masses and adiabaticity

evidence.quote: In the ASCC method, it just means that the collective kinetic energy term higher than the second order in the power-series expansion with respect to the collective momentum is omitted and, in contrast to the adiabatic perturbation, the smallness of the collective kinetic energy in comparison with the intrinsic two-quasiparticle excitation energies is not indispensable.
Therefore, it is also interesting to make a systematic comparison between different collective masses including the ASCC, cranking, GCM-GOA and ATDHFB collective masses.

accepted.question_text: What microscopic mechanism determines the collective mass along a large-amplitude collective path, in particular how do pairing correlations, repeated level crossings near the Fermi surface, nucleon-pair hopping, and smooth changes of single-particle wave functions combine to set the inertia against changing the collective coordinate?

evidence.quote: What is the microscopic mechanism of determining the collective mass ? This is one of the central questions in our study of many-body dynamics of the LACM.
To deepen our understanding of the collective mass of LACM, it is desirable to make a comprehensive analysis of the microscopic mechanism determining it.

accepted.question_text: How can one microscopically derive the full five-dimensional Bohr-Mottelson quadrupole collective Hamiltonian by extending a one-dimensional collective path to a two-dimensional collective hypersurface that can be mapped onto the beta-gamma plane, while also evaluating rotational moments of inertia at non-equilibrium points in a fully self-consistent way?

evidence.quote: Extending the one-dimensional (1D) collective path to the two-dimensional (2D) hypersurface and map it on the (β, γ) plane, we shall be able to microscopically derive the five-dimensional (5D) quadrupole collective Hamiltonian of Bohr and Mottelson [15].
The microscopic derivation of the Bohr-Mottelson collective Hamiltonian is a well-known long-standing subject in nuclear structure physics, but we are still on the way to the goal.

accepted.question_text: How can a microscopic theory of large-amplitude collective motion be extended to high-spin states so that it self-consistently includes the variation of intrinsic structure caused by rapid rotation, rather than remaining limited to low-spin states where those rotationally induced intrinsic changes can be neglected?

evidence.quote: Therefore, the range of its applicability is limited to low-spin states.

It remains as a future challenge to construct microscopic theory of LACM at high spin, which is capable of self-consistently taking into account variation of intrinsic structure due to rapid rotation.

accepted.question_text: How can large-amplitude collective-motion calculations be made systematic with improved nuclear energy density functionals while also developing numerical algorithms efficient enough to solve the moving-frame HFB and moving-frame QRPA equations iteratively along one-dimensional collective paths and especially over two-dimensional collective hypersurfaces?

evidence.quote: It is certainly a great challenge to make a systematic microscopic calculation for LACM phenomena using better energy density functionals.
For carrying out such ambitious calculations, it is certainly necessary to develop efficient numerical algorithms to solve the basic equations of the LACM theory.

accepted.question_text: What non-perturbative microscopic framework can describe large-amplitude collective motion in odd-A nuclei, or more generally in systems with several quasiparticles present, while treating the interplay between single-particle motion and collective motion in a unified way rather than starting from a small-amplitude particle-vibration-coupling approximation?

evidence.quote: In fact, microscopic description of LACM in odd-A nuclei remains as a vast unexplored field.
Non-perturbative method capable of treating LACM in odd-A nuclei (generally speaking, LACM in the presence of several quasiparticles) is lacking, however.

accepted.question_text: How should one build a microscopic theory of large-amplitude collective motion at finite temperature, and what microscopic mechanisms govern damping and dissipation of those motions as one moves from yrast states toward the compound-nucleus regime?

evidence.quote: Another vast unexplored field is the microscopic study of LACM at finite temperature.
Microscopic mechanism of damping and dissipation of various kinds of LACM is a long-term subject.

accepted.question_text: For tunneling decay from high-K to low-K isomers, which decay path dominates: the path through large-amplitude collective motion in the triaxial shape degree of freedom or the path through motion in the orientation degree of freedom of the angular-momentum vector relative to the principal axes of the body-fixed frame?
accepted.context_brief: Competing decay paths for high-K isomers

evidence.quote: The tunneling decay from high-K to low-K isomers is also interesting [65], because it poses a unique question as to which of the two competing decay paths dominates; one through LACM in the triaxial shape degree of freedom and the other in the orientation degree of freedom of the angular momentum vector (with respect to the principal axes of the body-fixed frame).

accepted.question_text: What happens when the amplitude of the wobbling mode in a rapidly rotating nucleus grows beyond the small-amplitude regime and the uniformly rotating nucleus becomes unstable with respect to that collective rotational degree of freedom, and how can microscopic large-amplitude collective-motion theory be applied to that regime as well as to chiral vibrations connecting right-handed and left-handed triaxial configurations?

evidence.quote: It is an interesting open problem to explore what will happen when the amplitude of the wobbling mode increases and the uniformly rotating nucleus becomes unstable against this collective rotational degree of freedom [68, 69].
It remains for the future to apply the microscopic LACM theory to these phenomena unique to rapidly rotating nuclei with triaxial shape.

accepted.question_text: How does rapid rotation modify large-amplitude tunneling and vibrational dynamics associated with broken reflection symmetry, including tunneling between left- and right-handed reflection-breaking configurations, transitional motion toward static octupole deformation, and large-amplitude fluctuations toward exotic shapes such as banana-shaped or tetrahedral configurations when the relevant potential-energy surfaces are shallow?

evidence.quote: Thus, it is quite interesting to investigate, on the basis of the microscopic LACM theory, how the quantum tunneling motion between the left- and right-configurations is affected by rapid rotation.
The potential energy surface is shallow, however, indicating that we need to take into account the large-amplitude tetrahedral shape fluctuation.
